question: How does the Gospel of Matthew begin its opening record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ?
opt1: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
opt2: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, as it is written in the prophets.
opt3: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
opt4: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things.
correct: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
explanation: Matthew opens with the royal and covenantal lineage of Jesus Christ: Matthew 1:1 (KJV) - "The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham."

question: Which four women are specifically mentioned by name in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in Matthew 1:3-6 before Mary?
opt1: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, and Leah
opt2: Thamar, Rachab, Ruth, and her that had been the wife of Urias (Bathsheba)
opt3: Miriam, Deborah, Hannah, and Huldah
opt4: Elisabeth, Anna, Salome, and Susanna
correct: Thamar, Rachab, Ruth, and her that had been the wife of Urias (Bathsheba)
explanation: Matthew 1:3-6 highlights God's grace by including four notable women in the ancestral line: Matthew 1:5 (KJV) - "And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;"

question: Into how many distinct generational spans of fourteen generations each does Matthew divide the genealogy from Abraham to Christ?
opt1: Two spans of fourteen generations
opt2: Four spans of fourteen generations
opt3: Three spans of fourteen generations
opt4: Seven spans of seven generations
correct: Three spans of fourteen generations
explanation: Matthew 1:17 structures the genealogy into three symmetrical periods of fourteen generations: Matthew 1:17 (KJV) - "So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations."

question: When Joseph discovered that his espoused wife Mary was with child of the Holy Ghost, what did he initially intend to do, being a just man?
opt1: To denounce her openly before the council of the Sanhedrin
opt2: To deliver her to the priest for the trial of jealousy
opt3: To demand the return of the dowry from her father's house
opt4: not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily
correct: not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily
explanation: Matthew 1:19 portrays Joseph's righteousness and merciful discretion: Matthew 1:19 (KJV) - "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

question: What reason did the angel of the Lord give unto Joseph in a dream for naming the child JESUS?
opt1: for he shall save his people from their sins
opt2: for he shall reign upon the throne of David for ever
opt3: for he shall overcome the heathen with an iron rod
opt4: for he shall restore the kingdom unto Israel
correct: for he shall save his people from their sins
explanation: Matthew 1:21 reveals the salvific purpose embedded in the sacred name Jesus: Matthew 1:21 (KJV) - "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins."

question: Which prophetic promise from Isaiah 7:14 does Matthew cite as fulfilled in the virginal conception of Christ?
opt1: Unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given
opt2: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us
opt3: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem
opt4: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light
correct: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us
explanation: Matthew 1:22-23 records the fulfillment of Isaiah's virgin birth prophecy: Matthew 1:23 (KJV) - "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

question: How did the angel of the Lord address Joseph when appearing unto him in a dream concerning Mary?
opt1: Joseph, thou servant of the Most High
opt2: Joseph, thou righteous carpenter of Nazareth
opt3: Joseph, thou son of David
opt4: Joseph, thou heir of the covenant
correct: Joseph, thou son of David
explanation: Matthew 1:20 highlights Joseph's Davidic lineage through the angelic greeting: Matthew 1:20 (KJV) - "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

question: According to Matthew 1:25, how did Joseph act in obedience regarding Mary until she brought forth her firstborn son?
opt1: He sent her unto the hill country of Judaea to dwell with Elisabeth
opt2: He offered two turtledoves at the temple in Jerusalem
opt3: He brought her to Bethlehem before the enrollment of Augustus
opt4: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS
correct: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS
explanation: Matthew 1:25 confirms Joseph's reverent restraint and prompt naming of the child: Matthew 1:25 (KJV) - "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

question: In the genealogy of Christ, who is named as the father of Joseph the husband of Mary?
opt1: Jacob
opt2: Heli
opt3: Matthan
opt4: Eleazar
correct: Jacob
explanation: Matthew 1:16 records Jacob as the father of Joseph: Matthew 1:16 (KJV) - "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

question: At what pivotal national epoch does the second division of fourteen generations conclude in Matthew's genealogy?
opt1: At the dedication of Solomon's temple
opt2: about the time they were carried away to Babylon
opt3: At the rebuilding of the walls under Nehemiah
opt4: At the victory of the Maccabees over the Greeks
correct: about the time they were carried away to Babylon
explanation: Matthew 1:11 marks the Babylonian exile as the turning point of the second genealogical grouping: Matthew 1:11 (KJV) - "And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon:"

question: During the reign of which king was Jesus born in Bethlehem of Judaea when wise men came from the east to Jerusalem?
opt1: Caesar Augustus
opt2: Herod Antipas
opt3: Herod the king
opt4: Archelaus
correct: Herod the king
explanation: Matthew 2:1 dates the arrival of the Magi during the reign of Herod the Great: Matthew 2:1 (KJV) - "Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,"

question: What precise inquiry did the wise men make upon arriving at Jerusalem, which troubled Herod and all Jerusalem with him?
opt1: Where is the prophet like unto Moses that shall arise in these days?
opt2: Where is the high priest that shall purify the sanctuary of God?
opt3: Where is the star of David that hath appeared in the heavens?
opt4: Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him
correct: Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him
explanation: Matthew 2:2 records the question of the Magi that alarmed King Herod: Matthew 2:2 (KJV) - "Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him."

question: When Herod demanded of the chief priests and scribes where Christ should be born, which prophetic passage did they quote?
opt1: And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel
opt2: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come
opt3: Behold, the Lord whom ye seek shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant
opt4: There shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel
correct: And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel
explanation: Matthew 2:5-6 cites the famous prophecy of Micah 5:2 concerning Bethlehem: Matthew 2:6 (KJV) - "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel."

question: What three royal gifts did the wise men present unto the young child after falling down and worshiping Him?
opt1: Silver, frankincense, and precious stones
opt2: gold, and frankincense, and myrrh
opt3: Purple garments, spikenard, and cedar oil
opt4: Crown of gold, ivory sceptre, and pure olive oil
correct: gold, and frankincense, and myrrh
explanation: Matthew 2:11 records the threefold gifts presented by the Magi: Matthew 2:11 (KJV) - "And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh."

question: Why did the wise men depart into their own country another way rather than returning to Herod in Jerusalem?
opt1: Because the roads of Judaea were blocked by Roman legions
opt2: Because they feared the robbers along the Jericho road
opt3: And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod
opt4: Because the star guided them directly across the wilderness of Edom
correct: And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod
explanation: Matthew 2:12 reveals divine intervention guiding the Magi to avoid Herod: Matthew 2:12 (KJV) - "And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way."

question: Whither was Joseph commanded by the angel of the Lord to flee with the young child and his mother to escape Herod's wrath?
opt1: Unto the mountains of Galilee
opt2: Unto the city of Damascus in Syria
opt3: Unto the desert caves of En-gedi
opt4: Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt
correct: Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt
explanation: Matthew 2:13 gives the angelic directive to flee into Egypt: Matthew 2:13 (KJV) - "And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him."

question: Which prophetic statement from Hosea 11:1 was fulfilled when Joseph brought Jesus out of Egypt after Herod's death?
opt1: Out of Egypt have I called my son
opt2: He shall be called a Nazarene
opt3: The Lord hath chosen Zion for his habitation
opt4: A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel
correct: Out of Egypt have I called my son
explanation: Matthew 2:15 cites the prophetic fulfillment of Israel's exodus typified in Christ: Matthew 2:15 (KJV) - "And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son."

question: What tragic slaughter did Herod decree in Bethlehem and all the coasts thereof when he saw he was mocked of the wise men?
opt1: He slew all the male priests who served at the local altars
opt2: sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under
opt3: He burned every dwelling whose inhabitants claimed Davidic descent
opt4: He took captive all firstborn sons into perpetual servitude
correct: sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under
explanation: Matthew 2:16 details Herod's murderous massacre of the infants: Matthew 2:16 (KJV) - "Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men."

question: Which Old Testament prophecy from Jeremiah 31:15 is cited as fulfilled by the lamentation of the mothers in Bethlehem?
opt1: The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord
opt2: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel
opt3: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not
opt4: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief
correct: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not
explanation: Matthew 2:17-18 links the slaughter in Bethlehem to Jeremiah's oracle of Rachel weeping: Matthew 2:18 (KJV) - "In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not."

question: Why did Joseph turn aside into the parts of Galilee and dwell in Nazareth rather than returning to Judaea after leaving Egypt?
opt1: Because the temple in Jerusalem was under Roman guard
opt2: Because the trade route through Samaria was closed due to famine
opt3: Because an angel commanded him to build a house in Capernaum
opt4: when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream
correct: when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream
explanation: Matthew 2:22 explains the historical and providential reasons for the holy family settling in Nazareth: Matthew 2:22 (KJV) - "But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:"

question: What central proclamation did John the Baptist preach in the wilderness of Judaea according to Matthew 3:1-2?
opt1: Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
opt2: Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come.
opt3: The time of the Gentiles is fulfilled; arise and take up your arms.
opt4: Behold the temple of the Lord, let all the earth keep silence before him.
correct: Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
explanation: Matthew 3:2 introduces the kingdom proclamation of John the Baptist: Matthew 3:2 (KJV) - "And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."

question: How did John the Baptist fulfill the prophecy spoken by the prophet Esaias (Isaiah 40:3)?
opt1: He built an altar of twelve unhewn stones in the Jordan valley
opt2: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
opt3: He blew the great silver trumpet at the dawn of the Sabbath
opt4: He stood on Mount Gerizim and proclaimed the blessings of the covenant
correct: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
explanation: Matthew 3:3 identifies John as the prophetic voice crying in the wilderness: Matthew 3:3 (KJV) - "For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight."

question: What was John the Baptist's clothing and sustenance while ministering in the wilderness?
opt1: A coat of fine linen with a woolen mantle; and his food was unleavened bread and figs
opt2: A sheepskin vesture with sandals of badger skin; and his food was barley loaves and oil
opt3: his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey
opt4: A sacerdotal tunic with pomegranates and bells; and his food was the showbread of the altar
correct: his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey
explanation: Matthew 3:4 describes the austere prophetic lifestyle of John: Matthew 3:4 (KJV) - "And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey."

question: What sharp rebuke did John address unto the Pharisees and Sadducees when he saw them come to his baptism?
opt1: Woe unto you, hypocrites, who devour widows' houses and make long prayers
opt2: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel
opt3: Ye rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah, who hath delivered you?
opt4: O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
correct: O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
explanation: Matthew 3:7 records John's piercing rebuke to the religious leaders: Matthew 3:7 (KJV) - "But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?"

question: What solemn warning did John give regarding presumptuous reliance upon biological descent from Abraham?
opt1: God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham
opt2: Abraham knoweth you not, and Isaac hath disowned your seed
opt3: The covenant of circumcision is broken by your deceitful traditions
opt4: Only they that keep the whole law shall inherit the promises of Abraham
correct: God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham
explanation: Matthew 3:9 refutes ethnic presumption with God's sovereign power: Matthew 3:9 (KJV) - "And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham."

question: According to Matthew 3:10, what decisive impending judgment is declared concerning every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit?
opt1: Its branches shall be pruned and cast outside the vineyard wall
opt2: is hewn down, and cast into the fire
opt3: It shall be left barren as a perpetual sign to all travelers
opt4: Its root shall dry up beneath the scorching wind of the east
correct: is hewn down, and cast into the fire
explanation: Matthew 3:10 emphasizes immediate accountability with the axe laid to the root: Matthew 3:10 (KJV) - "And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire."

question: How does John contrast his baptism with the baptism that the mightier One coming after him would administer?
opt1: John with water from Jordan; He with oil of gladness and wine of the covenant
opt2: John with tears of sorrow; He with the trumpet of victory and the crown of life
opt3: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he... shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire
opt4: John with the law of Moses; He with grace and truth upon Mount Zion
correct: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he... shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire
explanation: Matthew 3:11 declares the superior spiritual baptism administered by Christ: Matthew 3:11 (KJV) - "I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:"

question: What agricultural metaphor does John use in Matthew 3:12 to depict Christ's final eschatological separation of the righteous from the wicked?
opt1: Reaping the ripe vineyard and treading the great winepress outside the city
opt2: Shearing the unblemished sheep and driving the unruly goats into the rocks
opt3: Plucking the good figs into baskets and trampling the wild thorns underfoot
opt4: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire
correct: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire
explanation: Matthew 3:12 portrays Christ's thorough purging of the threshingfloor: Matthew 3:12 (KJV) - "Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire."

question: When John hesitated to baptize Jesus, saying 'I have need to be baptized of thee', what profound answer did Jesus give?
opt1: Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.
opt2: Allow it now, that the Scriptures of the prophets may be confirmed before this multitude.
opt3: For the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister and give his life.
opt4: Let it be done according to the law, that no man may find fault in my ministry.
correct: Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.
explanation: Matthew 3:15 reveals Christ's dedication to fulfilling all divine covenant righteousness: Matthew 3:15 (KJV) - "And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him."

question: What divine phenomena accompanied Jesus' emergence out of the water at His baptism in the Jordan?
opt1: A pillar of cloud rested upon the river and fire fell from heaven upon the bank
opt2: the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove... and lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased
opt3: The waters of Jordan stood on an heap as in the days of Joshua and angels sang
opt4: A rainbow appeared over the river and John fell upon his face worshiping
correct: the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove... and lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased
explanation: Matthew 3:16-17 records the glorious Trinitarian revelation at Christ's baptism: Matthew 3:17 (KJV) - "And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."

question: By whom was Jesus led up into the wilderness immediately following His baptism, and for what purpose?
opt1: By the angel Gabriel to receive the heavenly scrolls
opt2: By John the Baptist to fast and pray before entering the cities
opt3: led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil
opt4: By His own zeal to fulfill the forty years of Israel's wanderings
correct: led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil
explanation: Matthew 4:1 emphasizes the sovereign initiative of the Spirit leading Jesus into the wilderness: Matthew 4:1 (KJV) - "Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil."

question: With what Scripture from Deuteronomy 8:3 did Jesus defeat Satan's first temptation to command that stones become bread?
opt1: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want
opt2: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee
opt3: He humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna
opt4: It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
correct: It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
explanation: Matthew 4:4 records Jesus quoting Deuteronomy 8:3 to assert spiritual dependence on God: Matthew 4:4 (KJV) - "But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God."

question: When Satan set Jesus on a pinnacle of the temple and misused Psalm 91, what Scripture from Deuteronomy 6:16 did Jesus cite in response?
opt1: It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
opt2: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him.
opt3: He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
opt4: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
correct: It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
explanation: Matthew 4:7 refutes presumption by citing Deuteronomy 6:16: Matthew 4:7 (KJV) - "Jesus said unto him, It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God."

question: What condition did the devil demand on an exceeding high mountain in exchange for all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them?
opt1: Bow down before the golden image erected on the mountain
opt2: All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
opt3: Renounce the throne of David and rule over the Gentiles only
opt4: Divide the dominion of the earth equally between light and darkness
correct: All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
explanation: Matthew 4:9 exposes Satan's ultimate blasphemous desire for worship: Matthew 4:9 (KJV) - "And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me."

question: With what authoritative command and citation from Deuteronomy 6:13 did Jesus banish the devil in Matthew 4:10?
opt1: Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire prepared for the devil
opt2: The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan; even the Lord that hath chosen Jerusalem
opt3: Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
opt4: Touch not the anointed of God, and do his prophets no harm
correct: Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
explanation: Matthew 4:10 shows Jesus dismissing Satan with scripture: Matthew 4:10 (KJV) - "Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve."

question: When Jesus heard that John was cast into prison, to which region and city did He depart to fulfill the prophecy of Isaiah 9:1-2?
opt1: He went to Hebron in the hill country of Judaea
opt2: He departed into Samaria and dwelt in Sychar near Jacob's well
opt3: He withdrew into the wilderness of Bethabara beyond Jordan
opt4: he departed into Galilee; and leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim
correct: he departed into Galilee; and leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim
explanation: Matthew 4:12-13 highlights Christ's strategic ministry base in Capernaum: Matthew 4:13 (KJV) - "And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:"

question: How did Matthew summarize the inaugural preaching message of Jesus from the time He arrived in Galilee?
opt1: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
opt2: The year of the Lord's favour is come; arise and rejoice.
opt3: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord.
opt4: Believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.
correct: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
explanation: Matthew 4:17 notes that Jesus took up the identical kingdom message preached by John: Matthew 4:17 (KJV) - "From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."

question: What transformative invitation did Jesus extend unto Simon called Peter and Andrew his brother while they were casting a net into the sea?
opt1: Leave your father Zebedee and receive eternal life in my name
opt2: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
opt3: Go ye into all the cities of Galilee and preach the kingdom
opt4: Sell all that ye have and distribute to the poor along the shore
correct: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
explanation: Matthew 4:19 contains the iconic call of the first disciples: Matthew 4:19 (KJV) - "And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."

question: Whom did Jesus call next as disciples immediately after Peter and Andrew, while they were in a ship mending their nets?
opt1: Philip and Nathanael
opt2: Matthew the publican and Thomas called Didymus
opt3: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother
opt4: Simon the Canaanite and Judas Iscariot
correct: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother
explanation: Matthew 4:21 details the calling of the sons of Zebedee: Matthew 4:21 (KJV) - "And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them."

question: What threefold ministry activities characterized Jesus' itinerary throughout all Galilee according to Matthew 4:23?
opt1: Baptizing converts, ordaining priests, and rebuking the Roman centurions
opt2: Building synagogues, translating the scriptures, and collecting tithes for the poor
opt3: Offering sacrifices in the temple, celebrating holy feasts, and fasting forty days
opt4: teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people
correct: teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people
explanation: Matthew 4:23 summarizes the holistic threefold ministry of Jesus: Matthew 4:23 (KJV) - "And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people."

question: What blessing is promised to the poor in spirit in the opening Beatitude of the Sermon on the Mount?
opt1: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
opt2: for they shall inherit the earth.
opt3: for they shall obtain mercy.
opt4: for they shall see God.
correct: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
explanation: Matthew 5:3 opens the Beatitudes with the promise of the kingdom: Matthew 5:3 (KJV) - "Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."

question: Which specific Beatitude promises that the recipients 'shall inherit the earth'?
opt1: Blessed are they that mourn
opt2: Blessed are the meek
opt3: Blessed are the merciful
